results.title: Court acquits Adu-Boahene on two of 11 counts, orders defence in GH¢49.1m case
results.content: The Accra High Court has given former National Signals Bureau (NSB) Director-General Kwabena Adu-Boahene and his wife, Angela Adjei-Boateng, three weeks to file witness statements if they wish to testify in their defence in the GH¢49.1 million cyber-defence case. The statements are to be filed on or before December 4, 2026. The court also ordered the accused persons to open their defences on the remaining charges, while acquitting and discharging Adu-Boahene on two counts following a submission of no case to answer filed by the defence. The case has been adjourned to December 10, 2026, at 9:30 a.m. for continuation.

results.title: Ntim Fordjour alleges $3bn worth of narcotics linked to Ghana seized abroad since Mahama took office

results.title: Manhyia South MP allowed to retrieve passport as court varies bail terms
results.content: The High Court in Accra has varied the bail conditions of Manhyia South Member of Parliament, Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, allowing him to retrieve his passport from the court registry. The Commercial Court 5 Division granted the application on Thursday, November 12, 2026, during proceedings in the MP’s trial over allegations of causing financial loss to the state and money laundering. His lawyer, Samuel Atta Akyea, urged the court to approve the request, arguing that his client had no intention of fleeing the country. He also cited parliamentary rules requiring MPs to attend sittings, warning that prolonged absence without the Speaker’s written permission and a reasonable explanation could put the legislator’s seat at risk.

results.title: Health Ministry warns public against fraudulent Mercy Ships fundraising campaign
results.content: The Ministry of Health has warned the public against a fraudulent fundraising campaign being aired on some Ghanaian television stations, which falsely solicits money from people seeking surgical treatment through Mercy Ships.

results.title: Akufo-Addo appointed head of ECOWAS observer mission for Nigeria’s 2027 elections
results.content: Former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo will lead a 200-member ECOWAS Election Observation Mission to Nigeria ahead of the country’s January 16, 2027, general elections.
